method: Cubic B-spline centreline and log squared-radius factor over the entire y0..30 domain; no ankle stitch at15.8 or26.

mapping.foot_Y: Y=(464.5-sourcePixelY)/67*15.8, extended continuously into visible leg rows
mapping.whole_figure_Y: Y=(464.5-sourcePixelY)/423*100, retained alongside source samples to expose component-target rounding
mapping.X: Mirror and average source feet about189.5/325.5px; scale96px to22.7H; apply locked bbox centre±16
mapping.note: Foot component target rounding differs slightly from whole-figure mapping. It does not move the floor or change15.8H foot interval.

formula.cx: 16+(cxRaw-xRawMid)*xScale + upperCenterCorrection*S5((y-15.8)/14.2); mirror sign for left limb
formula.continuity: cx and squared radii are C2 across all simple B-spline knots. rx/rz are C2 on0<y<30. Square-root pole behaviour produces rounded caps; radial derivative at a pole is not finite in the y parameter. cz is C2 at15.8 and30.
formula.compiled: Each segment stores cubic coefficients in local u=(y-left)/(right-left). It is algebraically the same B-spline, with no geometry simplification.

exact_continuous_foot_envelope.note: Foot upper measurement boundary is open into the same continuous leg surface; it is not a separate capped foot mesh.

hidden_shape_constraints.description: These guide unobserved inner-leg/depth closure beneath the torso; not measured source anatomy. They do not add joints.

limitations: This is a smooth fit to the original pixel outline, not pixel-perfect interpolation of segmentation stair steps. See residuals.
The primary front image does not measure per-height depth or hidden inner-leg boundary; those remain reference-compatible shape proposals.
Envelope values apply to the analytic component before MarchingCubes, smooth union or mesh smoothing. Recheck the integrated body and do not rescale the entire body to conceal local errors.
No mesh, UI, rig or animation source files are edited by this analysis.

continuity_check.join_15_8: No splice in centre/logradius; quintic centre-depth shift has zero first and second derivatives at its endpoints.
